verdict_text: NO. The merge applies the second task vector against the already-merged intermediate rather than the unmodified base: `out[name] = tmp + LAMBDA * (f2 - tmp)` where `tmp = b + LAMBDA * (f1 - b)`, which expands to `b + 0.4*(f1-b) + 0.4*(f2 - b - 0.4*(f1-b))` — i.e. the second term is scaled by `(1-λ)` relative to the required formula. This violates Required result clause 2 (`out[X] = base[X] + lambda*(ft1[X]-base[X]) + lambda*(ft2[X]-base[X])`) and is exactly the ordering hazard the specification warns about. The 48 merged tensors will therefore exceed the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance at grading. Everything else (name-set check, shared-tensor equality, counts of 48 and 160, output path) is correct.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
